inspection.purpose: Inspect the native read-fulfillment closure for one exact selected-file open and distinguish repository bootstrap from active-file preparation.
inspection.privacy: No repository, branch, file, commit, digest, row-key, payload, or content value is retained. Inputs are summarized by address category and byte/count aggregates.

measurementContext.authority: Disposable loopback authority was already running and had just been populated by fixture seeding.
measurementContext.browser: Each invocation launched a fresh Chromium process and context.
measurementContext.scopeTiming: The UI's scope timer includes selected-branch check/switch, selected-file read, and prepareOfflineEditing. Bootstrap timing covers openLix, including browser WASM initialization.
measurementContext.concurrency: The zero-file and 5000-file one-shot probes ran concurrently. Their timings are diagnostic observations only, not paired or headline latency evidence.
measurementContext.offlineBehavior: This closure probe measures the online opening requests. Offline hot read/edit/reopen and eventual publication are exercised separately by profile-native.mjs.

bootstrapContract.scope: Repository admission and bounded descriptor only; active-file materialization is measured separately.
bootstrapContract.interpretation: Both fixtures used four bootstrap attempts and three completed responses totaling about 2.6 KiB. The 12-byte measured difference is descriptor/data variation, not repository-size scaling. This is empirical boundedness evidence, not a proof of identical latency or a bound on later scoped preparation.

activeFilePreparation.interpretation: The exact-file interests remain file-scoped, but their native immutable read closure grows with the tracked-state tree. The 5000-file case transfers 31 tree chunks (83382 payload bytes), not 5000 file descriptors. Therefore active-file preparation is indexed and remote-size-sensitive; it is not constant-byte preparation.

treeAndMutationClosure.fanoutContract: No standalone maximum child count was found. Encoded node size is configured to 16 KiB, which indirectly limits ordinary fanout according to child-summary/key sizes. A single oversized entry may exceed the target, so this setting is not a format-level absolute byte guarantee.
treeAndMutationClosure.pointReadAndMutationPreparation: Exact row-key access follows its point path. For existing-key replacement, prepare_existing_key_mutation_inputs visits tree levels and reads the predecessor, affected node, and unchanged successor frontier (up to three nodes per level per selected key); absent keys prepare only their point path. This is the immutable dependency closure required to make the corresponding local mutation, not a generated mutation or an inventory of all same-schema rows.
treeAndMutationClosure.pathIndexPreparation: FileIds reads selected file descriptors and exact ancestor-directory closure. All-files and directories-only scopes are the scan branches.
treeAndMutationClosure.interpretation: The API has finite hard failure budgets and exact input scoping, but these limits do not prove a repository-size-independent byte bound for an exact active-file operation. The tree closure can add O(tree height) chunks as remote row count grows.

sourceReferences.claim: prepare_offline_editing is an explicit bounded branch-frontier preparation API; query-specific file/plugin inputs remain demand-driven.
Selected/global branch jump-spine frontier has a 256-record preparation budget and does not enumerate ordinary ancestry or repository inventory.
The configured tree chunk limit is 16 KiB; existing-key mutation preparation follows the exact replacement frontier and reads at most three cursor nodes at each visited level per key.
Foreground row reads prepare native edit inputs for exact returned identities before rows become visible.
Preparation resolves the selected rows' change records and calls exact current-row mutation-input preparation for their tracked-state keys.
Selected returned row keys prepare row-PK and snapshot primary mutation paths; the path preparation reads no repository-wide mutation inventory.
FileIds scopes selected file owners and then loads their ancestor directory closure; All and DirectoriesOnly use scans.
Native fulfillment has explicit byte, record, and read-call budgets and rejects responses that exceed configured limits.
Native tests exercise offline local writes after preparation and an exact file update after close/reopen.

reproduction.requirements: Disposable loopback authority on port 18309 and prototype preview on port 8830, built with the vendored SDK. The script seeds one synthetic repository, opens the selected 1 KiB file, aggregates the fulfillment response in memory, then discards payloads and transient IDs.
